newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa ends mixed, nearbys firmer with NY gain.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa ends mixed, nearbys firmer with NY gain.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures closed mixed, with nearby months turning higher late as New York futures rose to session highs.

July closed near its daily high, up six stg at 1,001 stg per tonne. September gained three to 1,022. Total volume stood at 5,462, with the bulk of activity seen in the afternoon. September was by far the most active contract with 2,335 trades. July followed with 1,524 contracts changing hands. All other months traded fewer than 1,000.

After opening softer and spending most of the day in slightly negative ground, the nearby months started to turn around with New York's firmer open. When CSCE contracts added to gains as traders aimed to fill a chart gap between $1,432 and $1,441, London followed and broke above Thursday and Friday's highs.

But most of the activity here was seen in switches. Traders said 500 July/September contracts were crossed at 21 stg. The July/September switch closed down three stg from Friday at 21 and September/December continued to hover on both sides of unchanged.

After cocoa's late solid comeback on Monday, traders were mixed on the near-term outlook. Though fears of more speculative liquidation, particularly before New York's first notice day on June 17, weighed on prices, traders could not ignore cocoa's resiliency near crucial support at the April 9 low of 980.
The 980-level held on June 5 and May 1 to form a triple bottom on daily charts.
Because of last week's failure to slide below 980, some traders said cocoa could regain its composure and retest its upside. Stiff July resistance was seen at 1,060.
But technical analysts and traders said if 980 finally gave way amid speculative sales, they did not see July's next solid support surfacing until about 950.
In options, 92 contracts changed hands. Eighty-two May 1998 1,050 stg calls traded and 10 July 950 puts.
